into.label: Present used where the future is required
into.desc: Present chosen for a distant, uncertain or probabilistic future the morphological future owns.

into.label: Future over-applied where a present-for-future is natural
into.desc: Morphological future used where Italian's present-for-near-future is idiomatic.

splits.note: Clean 2-way; the two tense_choice buckets ARE the two directions.

into.label: Imperfect used for a completed prior-to-prior event
into.desc: mangiava for 'had eaten': imperfect where the trapassato's completed-anteriority is required.

into.label: Trapassato used for an ongoing background state
into.desc: avevo mangiato quando sei entrato read as finished where an ongoing state was meant.

into.label: Modal/stative: imperfect where the bounded-event pp is meant
into.desc: Production side (sapere/potere): sapevo for seppi 'found out', potevo for potei 'managed'.

into.label: Modal/stative: pp where the ongoing-state imperfect is meant
into.desc: Production side, the reverse: the bounded pp where the ongoing ability/state imperfect was intended.

into.label: Modal/stative aspect misread (comprehension)
into.desc: Reading side (conoscere/volere/usage.polite): translating pp conoscere as 'knew' not 'met'; missing volli 'insisted' vs volevo; the polite-imperfect reading. Direction-neutral by design (a comprehension miss).
into.FLAG: READING-SIDE: gated on the open comprehension-arm question (v15). If the reading arm is declined, this half stays untagged like the other 16 deferred comprehension entries.

splits.note: Split TWICE per doctrine: production (bidirectional -> a mirror pair) vs reading (one, comprehension-gated). The messiest of the four; Architecture may collapse the production pair if live data doesn't separate the directions.

into.label: Real-condition pattern used for a counterfactual
into.desc: present indicative + future ('se ho tempo, verro') where the counterfactual imperfect-subjunctive + conditional is required. The genuine production error.
